[RLOW.6.1.7] **An operation on an interval lowers inside `FN_INTERVAL_CHECK`.**
No runtime holds an interval value: the compiler lowers each operation on one to
comparisons of its endpoints ([LINT.3.1.1], [LINT.3.2.1], [LINT.4.1],
[LINT.5.1], [LINT.6.1]). It must lower each such operation to
`FN_INTERVAL_CHECK(s₁, e₁, v)`, or to `FN_INTERVAL_CHECK(s₁, e₁, s₂, e₂, v)` for
an operation with two interval operands (`proto/builtin_fn.proto#BuiltinFn`),
where each `sᵢ .. eᵢ` is an interval operand and `v` is the lowered endpoint
comparison or component read. The check encloses `v`. It is never an operand of
an `and` beside it, where a `false` operand would absorb its fault ([LNUL.4.2]).

The engine evaluates `FN_INTERVAL_CHECK` as [LINT.7.2] evaluates `..`:

1. If no argument faults and every pair is valid, it yields `v`, `null` included.
2. Otherwise it yields one fault, chosen as [LNUL.4.2] chooses among faults, from
   the faults of its arguments and, for each pair whose endpoints are two values,
   neither `null`, that are not `s <= e`, a `ComputationError` of kind `DOMAIN`
   ([LERR.1.4.10]) whose offending operand is that pair's `s`, as [LERR.9.12]
   chooses it for `..`.

A `null` `v` does not prevent the check, as a `null` operand prevents a builtin's
operation ([LNUL.4.10]): the check is the `..` operation, which [LINT.7.2]
performs whatever the enclosing operation's other operand is. A pair with a
`null` endpoint is valid.

Where both endpoints of a pair are compile-time constants ([LEXP.8.8]) and
`s <= e`, the compiler may leave the pair out of the check, and lowers the
operation to `v` alone when no pair is left. It must not fold an operation over
an invalid interval to a value; an invalid interval of literals is refused
instead ([LINT.7.4]).
